This wouldn't work, for a few reasons:

1) Unlicensed wireless spectrum is extremely constrained and inadequate for this use case on a wide scale.

2) The 802.11 protocol has a severe flaw where it uses CSMA instead of TDMA. TDMA assigns a block of time to each connected client device to talk in turn, which allows it to scale to hundreds of connected devices. 802.11 uses CSMA which causes it to suffer drastic performance hits above 25-30 connected devices.

3) 802.11 doesn't use GPS sync. Which leads to massive interference issues because every access point is trying to tx/rx over other access points at the same time.

4) High bandwidth, obstruction penetration (walls, trees, hills, etc), cheap enough for consumers. Pick 1.

5) N/2 issues. For every additional hop out in a mesh, you lose half your bandwidth.

6) You need directional antennas ($$$ and technical know-how) or you'll create horrendous amounts of self-interference by using omnidirectional antennas.

TLDR: Mesh wireless networks are costly and hard to build even if one person controls the entire mesh. When every node is independent, it's like having 400 chiefs, no indians, and everyone shouting into a megaphone.
